posts.text: Jev introduces a new shape of LLM - System One, aka Decision Models. Last week TypeSafe AI unveiled Jev , their first example of a new category of model that they are calling "System One models" (I'm with Maggie Appleton, I think "decision models" is a better name for these). Jev is an interesting variant on the usual LLM format: it still accepts text inputs, but instead of text output it returns floating point numbers corresponding to categories, yes/no questions, ratings, and associated confidence scores. posts.text: Claude Opus 5.5 takes #1 on RSI Index and is the first model to beat the published reference on LM Training under our protocol, marking a major step forward for long-horizon agentic work.

posts.author: ValsAI
posts.text: On RSI Index, Opus 5.5 is the top model on four of the five research tasks. On LM Training, where the model trains its own small language model within a 24-hour budget, its result beat the published human baseline. This shifts our timeline for full RSI from August 2027 to July 2027. On Terminal Bench 4 it scores 61.6% vs 45.5% for Opus 5. On Proof Bench it ties for #1 at 100%, and is the cheapest

posts.author: ValsAI
posts.text: The gains extend to Program Bench where Opus 5.5 fully resolves 18.5% of tasks vs 7.0% for Fable 5.1, 5.5% for GPT-6 Astra and 3.0% for Opus 5. It resolves more than 6x Opus 5 at the same effort setting, while also finishing faster and at lower cost: 2.4 hours and $42.66/task vs 2.9 hours and $60.29.

posts.author: ValsAI
posts.text: It also improves on more everyday agentic work, taking #2 on Terminal Bench Science, SRE Bench, Mystery Mechanism, IOI, EMB, and Vibe Code Bench ahead of Opus 5 on all four. The clearest gains are around sustained execution, iteration and recovery.

posts.author: ValsAI
posts.text: The improvement is not uniform. Opus 5.5 regresses from Opus 5 on Med Code, Public Benefits, Legal Research, Tax Agent Bench, and HLAB, with the losses concentrated in retrieval, fidelity and rubric-following.

posts.author: ValsAI
posts.text: This model has 1M context window and 128K max output tokens. It was run on Anthropic's default provider settings: Temperature=1, default Top-P and Top-K, and max compute effort. RSI Index ran in native Claude Code at max effort.
